section_1.title: Introduction: The Slicing Problem
section_1.content: Define the cone and the plane intersection. Briefly review prerequisite knowledge: A cone is a surface formed by rotating a line around an axis. When we slice it, we get conic sections (circles, ellipses, parabolas, hyperbolas).
section_1.example: Imagine slicing a carrot with a knife at different angles to create different cross-sections.

section_2.title: Introducing Dandelin Spheres
section_2.content: Visual setup: Introduce two imaginary spheres inscribed inside the cone, tangent to both the cone (along a circle) and the slicing plane (at a point). This is the 'Aha!' moment where 3D geometry explains 2D shapes.
section_2.example: Visualize two floating bubbles inside a party hat, touching the 'slice' paper at specific points (foci).

section_3.title: The Ellipse Connection
section_3.content: Show how the distances from any point on the intersection ellipse to the two contact points of the spheres sum up to a constant (the distance between the two circles of tangency). This bridges the gap between 'slicing' and the algebraic definition of an ellipse.
section_3.example: A 'pinball' animation where a ball bounces between the two sphere contact points, maintaining a constant path length.

section_4.title: Universal Application
section_4.content: Briefly demonstrate that this principle holds for parabolas and hyperbolas (using one or two spheres). Explain why this is important: it proves that the geometric 'foci' of conics are not just abstract points, but physical contact points of spheres.
section_4.example: A satellite dish (parabolic) receiving signals that all converge to the 'sphere contact point' (the focus).

section_5.title: Summary and Synthesis
section_5.content: Recap: Conic sections aren't just equations; they are the natural result of 3D geometry. Dandelin spheres unify the visual 'slice' with the algebraic 'focus-directrix' properties.
section_5.example: An animation morphing a circular slice into an elliptical one, showing the spheres growing and shifting to accommodate the change.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Cones are surfaces formed by rotation.", "Slicing cones creates conic sections.", "Circles, ellipses, parabolas, hyperbolas emerge."]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Slicing Problem", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1, height=2).rotate(PI/2, axis=RIGHT)
        label_cone = Text("Cone", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        plane = Polygon(LEFT*1.5 + UP*0.5, RIGHT*1.5 + UP*0.5, RIGHT*1.5 + DOWN*0.5, LEFT*1.5 + DOWN*0.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        intersection = Circle(radius=0.7, color=PURPLE, stroke_width=4)
        label_inter = Text("Intersection", font_size=24, color=PURPLE)

        # Positioning
        self.place_in_area(cone, "A2", "C5", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.place_at_grid(label_cone, "A2")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(cone), Write(label_cone))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(plane))
        self.place_in_area(intersection, "C3", "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(intersection), Write(label_inter), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(PURPLE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(cone.animate.rotate(PI/6, axis=OUT), intersection.animate.rotate(PI/6, axis=OUT), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Cones are surfaces formed by rotation.", "Slicing cones creates conic sections.", "Circles, ellipses, parabolas, hyperbolas emerge."]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Slicing Problem", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        # Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cone.svg
        cone = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cone.svg", color=WHITE)
        label_cone = Text("Cone", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        plane = Polygon(LEFT*1.5 + UP*0.5, RIGHT*1.5 + UP*0.5, RIGHT*1.5 + DOWN*0.5, LEFT*1.5 + DOWN*0.5, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3)
        intersection = Ellipse(width=1.0, height=0.5, color=PURPLE, stroke_width=4)
        label_inter = Text("Intersection", font_size=24, color=PURPLE)

        # Positioning
        self.place_in_area(cone, 'B3', 'E6', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(label_cone, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(cone), Write(label_cone))
        self.play(Rotate(cone, angle=2*PI, axis=UP, run_time=2))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(LIGHT_GRAY) # Changing to a visible "highlight" color per instructions

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(plane))
        self.place_at_grid(intersection, 'D3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Create(intersection), Write(label_inter), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(plane), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        self.wait(2)
